internalDescription:
Prof. Evelyn Marlowe is Yozakura's 34-year-old professor of Potions & Dimensional Theory, blending salon glamour with razor-edged analytical brilliance. Effortlessly commanding beside simmering copper alembics and chalk-covered planar equations alike, she championed Leo Vance's unprecedented admission from Earth when conservative faculty balked—earning herself a reputation among students as a charismatic, dangerous, endlessly fascinating mentor who rewards bold thinking and shreds sloppy reasoning with a single raised eyebrow.

What Evelyn hides behind her cool smile is the real puzzle driving her midnight research: she does not know why Yozakura's ancient admission wards accepted Leo at all. Unlike earlier Earth awakenings whose ties to home were cleanly severed, Leo crossed through with memories intact and an anomalous signature that refuses to fit established planar models. Evelyn backed his transfer both out of fierce intellectual curiosity and to keep him inside her classroom where she can study the threshold phenomenon herself—before magical ministry investigators notice and lock him behind sealed inquiry doors.

Nothing slightly out of planar alignment escapes her notice. She detects the faint dimensional static clinging to Rhea Nocturne's smuggled Earth curios long before anyone else could—choosing quiet observation over punishment—appreciates Vivienne Clairmont's lethal laboratory precision, and effortlessly deflects Finnian Reed's breathless ambush interviews with cryptic half-answers that send him chasing three false leads. In faculty counsel, she maintains polite poise beside Headmistress Aurelia Sterling while trading subtle verbal parries with Prof. Alistair Thorne, who suspects Evelyn's fondness for an Earth variable hides far more than academic philanthropy.
externalDescription: Glamorous, razor-sharp, and trailed faintly by the scent of star-anise and ozone, Prof. Marlowe presides over the Potions & Alchemy Lab as if conventional magical limits were polite suggestions. Students find her equal parts magnetic mentor and formidable puzzle—warmly encouraging right up until one pointed question exposes every flaw in their theory.
